chunks: We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so that no soul will be wronged in the least; and even if it were equal to the weight of a mustard seed, We shall bring it forth. And sufficient are We as Reckoner.
ai.seo_question: How does God ensure perfect justice for even the smallest deeds on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Anbiya underscores the absolute precision of divine justice, where the 'scales' represent not just physical weight but the moral gravity of actions, ensuring no soul is wronged even by a fraction. The phrase 'We are sufficient as Reckoner' highlights God's direct, personal involvement in the accounting, a concept deeply resonant with the Shia belief in the infallible Imam as the interpreter of this justice. This emphasis on microscopic accountability serves as both a comfort to the righteous and a warning to the oppressors, reinforcing the theological principle of 'Adl (Divine Justice).
